item.title: Updated llm-echo Debug Plugin Simulates Token Usage for Tool Calls and System Prompts
item.description:
Updated llm-echo Debug Plugin Simulates Token Usage for Tool Calls and System Prompts

A developer has enhanced the llm-echo debug plugin to simulate token usage tracking for additional components in LLM interactions. The update enables more accurate cost and performance testing during development.

🔍 Overview

The llm-echo plugin acts as a non-LLM “model” that repeats input prompts verbatim. It serves as a testing tool for validating prompt structures and token accounting without invoking actual language models.

⚙️ Key details

  • Now tracks tokens for: tool calls, system prompts, and reasoning steps
  • Provides simulated input/output token counts in usage reports
  • Maintains existing functionality for echoing prompts and context

🧩 Example usage 

1

uvx --with llm-echo llm -m echo 'hi there' -o thinking 1 --usage

Output:

1
2
3
4
5
6
7
8
9

First I consider the prompt, then I decide what to say.
{
 "prompt": "hi there",
 "system": "",
 "attachments": [],
 "stream": true,
 "previous": []
}
Token usage: 2 input, 24 output

💡 Why it matters

This update allows developers to debug token consumption across more interaction elements, improving cost estimation and prompt optimization before deploying to real models.

#AIDevelopment #LLMTools #Debugging #TokenUsage

item.title: Epic Games previews AI‑assisted, faster launcher with Linux support
item.description:
Epic Games previews AI‑assisted, faster launcher with Linux support

Epic Games announced today a preview of a refreshed Epic Games Launcher that is “way faster” and adds Linux support.

🔍 Overview

  • The new launcher is described as “way faster” and “more responsive than the current one, and has a new look.”
  • It now supports Linux alongside Windows and Mac.
  • Epic says the refresh was “vibe coded.”

🛠️ AI involvement

  • Epic has been “making a big push into AI‑assisted development,” and this approach includes the new launcher.
  • Martin Keely, Epic’s VP and GM of the Epic Games Store and Epic Online Services, said “We used AI as a tool for this.”
  • AI has been “super helpful” for testing and for “replicating the core functionality from the existing launcher.”
  • Keely added that AI also enabled offering the launcher on Linux.
  • The team “definitely had agents write and review all of the code,” and “used it to replicate the core functionality.”
  • The development process was “managed that process” and “supervised the entirety of what we did.”
  • While the team has not adopted the “no more hand‑written code” model reported by Bloomberg, the effort “is on the same train” as the company’s broader AI pivot.

🚀 Availability

  • The new Epic Games Launcher preview is available on Windows, Mac, and Linux beginning today; the old version will remain available.
  • Epic also announced plans to bring Fortnite to Linux through the app.
  • No specific timeline for a full migration; Keely says the full launch will happen when the update feels “stable” and has parity in “all places that we need” with the current launcher.

📈 Why it matters

  • CEO Tim Sweeney announced a “huge pivot underway” to “move developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration.”
  • He emphasized the goal is “not to do the same stuff with fewer people, but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal.”
  • Sweeney noted the recent March layoffs of more than 1,000 staffers are “not related to AI,” and added, “To the extent it improves productivity, we want to have as many awesome developers developing great content and tech as we can.”

#EpicGames #AIdevelopment #LinuxGaming

Source: Epic’s new games launcher is ‘vibe coded’

item.title: Epic Games adopts AI‑first approach for Disney shooter, delaying release
item.description:
Epic Games adopts AI‑first approach for Disney shooter, delaying release

Epic Games announced that its unannounced Disney shooter will be built under an “AI‑first” mandate, pushing developers to use AI tools such as Anthropic’s Claude for both code and art. The project has been moved out of its original March release window.

🔍 Overview

  • Project: an unannounced shooter featuring characters from Marvel and Star Wars.
  • Collaboration: part of a multiyear partnership between Epic Games and Disney, which invested $1.5 billion in Epic in 2024.
  • Shift: developers have been given an “AI‑first” mandate to use tools like Anthropic’s Claude.

⚙️ AI‑first mandate

  • Developers were told to use AI tools such as Anthropic’s Claude.
  • One of the game’s directors said to staff, “No more hand‑written code.”
  • Staff were also told that all of the game’s art will be “generated with full AI workflows.”
  • Epic spokesperson Jake Jones said the company is “embracing AI‑accelerated development.”

📅 Timeline & status

  • Original target: March release window.
  • Current status: delayed beyond the March window (no new date provided).

💡 Why it matters

  • Shows large‑scale use of generative AI for both programming and visual content in a AAA title.
  • Epic already uses AI in Fortnite, which has previously featured Disney characters like an AI Darth Vader.
  • AI game‑development tools are also emerging from other large companies, such as Meta and Google.
  • Epic CEO Tim Sweeney has pushed for Steam to drop its “made with AI” tag, arguing that “AI will be involved in nearly all future production.”
  • Earlier this year, Epic laid off over 1,000 employees following a downturn in Fortnite engagement since 2025.

🛠️ Tools & workflow

AI Tool Intended Use
Anthropic’s Claude Generate code and create art assets

#EpicGames #AIdevelopment #DisneyGame #GameDev

Source: Epic shifts to ‘AI-accelerated development’ for upcoming Disney game

item.title: 500 AI Agents Projects Launches Curated Collection
item.description:
500 AI Agents Projects Launches Curated Collection

A new curated collection, the 500 AI Agents Projects, has been released, offering a comprehensive repository of AI agent use cases, implementations, and tutorials across industries and frameworks.

🔍 Overview

  • The 500 AI Agents Projects is a curated collection of 500+ AI agent projects, use cases, and working implementations.
  • It spans every major framework (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, Agno) and industry (Healthcare, Finance, Education, Cybersecurity, and more).
  • The repository is described as the most comprehensive collection of AI agent projects, use cases, and working implementations.

🧩 How it works

  • All agents in the agents/ directory are self-contained with their own requirements.txt and .env.example files.
  • No monorepo setup is required.
  • Users can run a working agent in under 5 minutes by following these steps: 
    1
2
3
4
5
6

    git clone https://github.com/ashishpatel26/500-AI-Agents-Projects.git
cd 500-AI-Agents-Projects
cd agents/01-web-research-agent
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env
python agent.py

⚙️ Key details

  • The repository provides navigation options for:

    • Running a working agent immediately via the agents/ directory.
    • Browsing use cases by AI framework or industry.
    • Comparing frameworks to choose the right one.
    • Contributing new agents.
    • Accessing a course on building AI agents.

  • Framework comparison for choosing the right tool:

Framework Best For Rating Notes
LangGraph Stateful workflows, RAG pipelines, complex graphs ⭐⭐⭐ ✅
CrewAI Role-based teams, business automation, rapid prototyping ⭐⭐ ✅
AutoGen Code generation, research, self-healing workflows ⭐⭐⭐ ✅
Agno Lightweight single agents, tool integration, fast iteration ⭐ ✅
LlamaIndex Document Q&A, enterprise RAG, data pipelines ⭐⭐ ⚠️
  • Recommended frameworks for specific use cases:
    • Just starting out → Agno or CrewAI
    • Need stateful graphs + RAG → LangGraph
    • Building code-writing / research agents → AutoGen
    • Enterprise document pipelines → LlamaIndex

🚀 Availability

  • The repository includes production examples, tutorials, and working code.
  • It showcases practical applications across sectors such as healthcare, finance, education, and retail.
  • Example projects include:
    • Healthcare: HIA (Health Insights Agent), AI Health Assistant
    • Finance: Automated Trading Bot, Agent Wallet SDK
    • Education: Virtual AI Tutor
    • Customer Service: 24/7 AI Chatbot
    • Retail: Product Recommendation Agent
    • Transportation: Self-Driving Delivery Agent

💡 Why it matters

  • The collection provides a centralized resource for developers to explore, learn, and implement AI agents across diverse domains.
  • It offers open-source projects with practical, ready-to-run implementations, reducing the barrier to entry for AI agent development.

#AIagents #OpenSource #AIdevelopment #Frameworks #UseCases #Tutorials

item.title: AgentGuide launches AI Agent development and job-seeking knowledge base
item.description:
AgentGuide launches AI Agent development and job-seeking knowledge base

A new open-source knowledge base, AgentGuide, has been introduced to provide a systematic, practical, and job-oriented solution for AI Agent development and career preparation.

🔍 Overview

AgentGuide positions itself as a one-stop solution for AI Agent development and job-seeking, offering a structured learning path, practical guidance, and career-focused insights. It integrates existing high-quality resources without reinventing the wheel, focusing on delivering actionable content.

🧩 How it works

  • Aggregates and organizes fragmented resources into a complete learning roadmap, clarifying the sequence of topics to study.
  • Provides job-seeking orientation by annotating each knowledge point with interview questions and resume-writing tips.
  • Covers the full AI Agent development stack, from model fine-tuning to deployment, without binding to a single framework.

⚙️ Key details

AgentGuide addresses common challenges in AI Agent development, including:

  • Long-task execution issues (early stopping, loops, state loss) and debugging difficulties.
  • Lack of a unified system architecture for concepts like LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, MCP, Skills, and Multi-Agent.
  • Integration of Context, Memory, Tools, Permissions, Sandbox, and Trace in reliable systems.
  • Gaps in RAG implementations for complex documents, multimodal data, citation tracing, evaluation sets, and online monitoring.
  • Missing baselines, metrics, failure analyses, and engineering trade-offs in project documentation.
  • Unclear skill and portfolio requirements for development, algorithm, Agentic RL, and research roles.
  • Rapid updates in papers, frameworks, and open-source projects, with guidance on prioritization and validation.

The project organizes content around four pillars:

  • 做得出 (Buildable): Capability to develop AI Agents.
  • 跑得稳 (Stable): Reliability in execution.
  • 测得准 (Measurable): Accurate evaluation and testing.
  • 讲得清 (Explainable): Clear communication of methods and results.

📚 Coverage

AgentGuide includes the following technical areas:

Agent / Workflow

  • LangGraph
  • OpenAI Agents SDK
  • AutoGen
  • CrewAI
  • Pydantic AI

Tools & Platforms

  • Dify
  • n8n
  • Flowise

Task Types

  • Research
  • Coding
  • Web Agent
  • Multi-Agent
  • Supervisor
  • Handoff
  • Computer Use
  • Browser Automation

Context Engineering

  • System
  • Memory
  • Retrieval
  • Trace
  • Context Compression
  • Prompt Cache

Tools & Protocols

  • Tool Schema
  • MCP
  • Skills

Reliability

  • Sandbox
  • HITL (Human-in-the-Loop)
  • Retry
  • Cost Guard

🚀 Availability

AgentGuide is an open-source knowledge base, actively updated with new content and community contributions.

#AIagents #AgentGuide #AIdevelopment #jobseeking #knowledgebase #systematiclearning

item.title: 🚀 Supercharge Your Coding: How Cursor AI & MCP Are Revolutionizing Development
item.description:
🚀 Supercharge Your Coding: How Cursor AI & MCP Are Revolutionizing Development

𝙎𝙪𝙢𝙢𝙖𝙧𝙮: Discover how Cursor AI’s intelligent code editor combined with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) creates a powerful development environment that streamlines coding, enhances productivity, and makes advanced AI accessible to developers of all skill levels.

🧠 Intelligent Coding Assistants: The Future is Here

Remember when coding meant staring at a blank screen, hoping for inspiration? Those days are rapidly disappearing as AI-powered coding tools transform how we write, debug, and deploy software. Two revolutionary technologies—Cursor AI and the Model Context Protocol (MCP)—are at the forefront of this transformation, promising to make developers more efficient while lowering the barrier to entry for AI-enhanced development.

But what exactly are these tools, and why should you care? Let’s explore how they work together to create a seamless, intelligent coding environment that might just change the way you approach your next project.

🖥️ Cursor AI: Your Intelligent Coding Companion

Cursor AI isn’t just another code editor—it’s your personal coding assistant integrated directly into your development environment. Think of it as having an experienced developer looking over your shoulder, offering suggestions, catching errors, and helping you write cleaner code faster.

𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗙𝗲𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗧𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗦𝗲𝘁 𝗖𝘂𝗿𝘀𝗼𝗿 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁:

  • 🔍 Code Autocompletion: Get real-time suggestions as you type, significantly boosting your productivity

  • 🐛 Error Detection: Automatically identifies potential bugs and issues before they become problems

  • 🔄 Code Refactoring: Simplifies and optimizes your code with minimal effort, ensuring maintainability

  • 📝 Documentation Assistance: Automatically generates code comments and explanations, saving you time

Setting up Cursor AI is refreshingly straightforward. Simply visit the official website, download the installer for your operating system, and follow the guided installation process. Within minutes, you’ll have access to a sleek, modern interface designed to make coding more intuitive and efficient.

🔄 MCP: The Context Bridge for AI Tools

The Model Context Protocol (MCP), developed by Anthropic, serves as the critical bridge between your code and its data sources. This standardized interface ensures that your AI models have the context they need to make informed decisions and provide accurate responses.

𝘞𝘩𝘺 𝘋𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘭𝘰𝘱𝘦𝘳𝘴 𝘈𝘳𝘦 𝘌𝘹𝘤𝘪𝘵𝘦𝘥 𝘈𝘣𝘰𝘶𝘵 𝘔𝘊𝘗:

  • 🧩 Context Management: Ensures AI models have access to the contextual information they need

  • 🔌 Plug-and-Play Integration: Eliminates complex configuration requirements

  • 📈 Enhanced Model Performance: Improves results, especially in natural language processing tasks

  • 🔄 Flexibility: Adapts to various data sources, structuring context to facilitate better learning and inference

The integration process is surprisingly simple. First, find an MCP server on platforms like Smithery AI, then copy the installation command. Within Cursor AI, navigate to settings, add a new MCP server, paste the command, and you’re ready to go.

🛠️ Creating a Powerful Workflow with Cursor AI and MCP

When combined, Cursor AI and MCP create a development environment that’s greater than the sum of its parts. Here’s what this powerful pairing offers different types of users:

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗡𝗲𝘄𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿𝘀:

The user-friendly interface and guided integration process make advanced AI accessible without requiring deep expertise. You’ll spend less time struggling with setup and more time learning and building.

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗨𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘀:

Enhanced productivity through better context management and streamlined workflows means you can develop and test applications faster than ever before.

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗘𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗽𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗲𝘀:

Teams benefit from greater efficiency, more consistent project outcomes, and robust testing capabilities, making these tools ideal for business environments where quality and speed matter.

Let’s see this in action. After configuring MCP with Cursor AI, you can test the integration by running a context-aware function. For example, using the “Sequential-Thinking MCP” to plan a game development project would result in a structured approach covering game concept, technical requirements, and game elements—without writing a single line of code yet.

🔗 Enhancing Your Stack with Apidog

While Cursor AI and MCP focus on improving your coding experience, adding Apidog to your toolkit can significantly enhance your API development and documentation workflow. This all-in-one platform offers powerful tools for designing, testing, and documenting APIs in a unified environment.

By incorporating Apidog alongside Cursor AI and MCP, you create a comprehensive development ecosystem that addresses every aspect of modern application development—from writing code to deploying and documenting APIs.

🌟 The Future of Development Is Here

The combination of Cursor AI and MCP represents a significant leap forward in how we approach software development. These tools don’t just make coding faster—they make it smarter, more accessible, and more enjoyable.

As AI continues to evolve, we can expect these tools to become even more sophisticated, further blurring the line between human and machine capabilities. The result? More intuitive coding experiences, fewer errors, and greater innovation across the development landscape.

The question isn’t whether you should adopt these technologies—it’s how quickly you can integrate them into your workflow to stay ahead of the curve. Are you ready to embrace the future of development?
